cases.rationale: A child is sitting on a carpeted floor. At the lower left, a partly cropped open laptop has an identifiable keyboard; a small colorful bound book lies at the upper right. The green background is hanging curtain fabric, not an identifiable couch, and the other small floor item has no identifiable category object features. No unresolved category ambiguity.

A batter and a partly cropped catcher are actual people. The catcher at the far left has a visible brown baseball fielding mitt. The bat, baseball clothing, dirt and grass do not supply other defined objects; ordinary clothing or equipment is not a tie or other listed category. No unresolved category ambiguity.

A kneeling man is handling a black dog whose body, muzzle and legs are visible, with another person standing behind the chain-link fence. The dog's raised pale paw and fur are not a flying disc. Grass, fence and a brick wall provide no other identifiable listed objects. No unresolved category ambiguity.

A red octagonal roadside sign bears readable STOP and additional lettering, establishing an actual stop sign. Utility poles, wires, trees, the hillside and sky contain no identifiable traffic signal, vehicle or other listed object. No unresolved category ambiguity.

People with exposed human faces are wearing furry bear costumes and riding a motorcycle with a sidecar; its handlebars, mirrors and vehicle body are visible. The costumes are neither actual bear animals nor teddy-bear toys, and their gloves are not baseball mitts. A tiny dark-and-light vehicle-like fragment in the upper-right background could be a passenger car, but its identity is unresolved (car unclear).

An airborne snowboarder is an actual person holding a white snowboard, identifiable by its broad continuous deck and boarding context. Another distant person is standing on the snow. The broad board is not skis, a skateboard or a surfboard, and trees and snow contain no other identifiable defined objects. No unresolved category ambiguity.

The cropped torso and legs belong to a person riding a red snowboard, whose broad deck is visible at the left amid snow. The lettering and logo on clothing/board are not actual depicted category objects. No other listed object is identifiable, and there is no unresolved category ambiguity.

A man holds a recognizable handleless drinking glass, which counts as cup rather than a stemmed wine glass. A white sink basin and its plumbing/faucet context are visible at the right, with a capped narrow-neck bottle above it. Dark wall panels are not identifiable television displays. No unresolved category ambiguity.

The plate holds egg, sauce and a thick round piece of ham, with diced browned potatoes and orange vegetable pieces behind it. The ham is not an identifiable frankfurter; the plate is not a bowl. Sandwich is unclear because any bread support beneath the egg and ham is obscured. Carrot is unclear because the orange pieces cannot be distinguished confidently from other orange vegetables. No other defined food or object is identifiable.

A child and a partial background adult are visible. The child holds a fork whose handle and tined head reach the mouth; it is not a spoon or toothbrush. The white surface at the lower right could be an eating table or a tray, so dining table remains unclear. The shirt buttons are not a tie, and no other defined object is identifiable.

A floral upholstered sofa and a dark single-person armchair are visible; a buttoned handheld remote rests on the armchair. The side-table stack has flat rectangular covers/edges but insufficient detail to establish bound books rather than cases or papers, so book is unclear. The lamp is not a vase, framed pictures do not establish actual people, and the pale decoration at the chair back does not establish an animal.

An actual elephant carries people, with another person alongside its head. Its trunk, large ear, hide and tusk establish elephant identity. Two distant grazing livestock animals are too small to resolve horse versus cattle, so horse and cow are unclear. Saddle pads and harness ropes do not establish a chair, bench, backpack or tie; no other defined objects are identifiable.
